analyst_view.overall: Hajduk Split (13th, 6 pts) host Sint-Truiden (10th, 7 pts) with both still in range of the knockout places, so neither side has a reason to hold back. Poljud is closed to regular fans after a UEFA punishment; about 8,000 invited children will sit in the east stand, with around 250 Sint-Truiden fans. Hajduk, top of the HNL after a 2-1 win at Lokomotiva, are without Hadzikadunic (counted), Pajaziti, Ivusic and Brajkovic, but winger Soticek (minor knock) and Sanyang (tired after Gambia duty) were only rested at the weekend and are back in contention. Sint-Truiden drew 2-2 at Charleroi under coach Jonas De Roeck and no absentees are reported. Italian referee Matteo Marchetti is named, and the numbers already trim cards about 7% for his record.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already adding about 6% to Sint-Truiden's goals for Hadzikadunic's absence. Both sides' recent scoring is in the momentum adjustment, and Soticek and Sanyang are back for Hajduk after being rested, so the attack is close to full strength and I stay at 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, with Hajduk's recent corner count nudged up and Sint-Truiden's down by momentum. The near-empty stadium and Soticek's return on the wing don't point clearly to more or fewer corners, so I stay at 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, already trimmed for referee Marchetti's low card record (-7%) and both sides' recent counts. I lean a little lower, to about 3.3: with Poljud closed to regular fans and only invited children and a couple of hundred away supporters in, there is far less crowd pressure on players and referee, which the numbers can't see.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots. Sint-Truiden's busy attacking and Hajduk's tight recent defending are both in the momentum adjustment, and the team news has no new absence that changes shot volume, so I stay at 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target, already trimmed for Hajduk conceding few on target lately (Sint-Truiden -7%). Hadzikadunic's absence is counted and nothing else in the news changes how often either side tests the goalkeeper, so I stay at 9.1.
